messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: AUTO-PAGER fired for route `/v1/generate` — p99 latency 2.8s (SLO 1.5s). PagerDuty incident PD-54321 created and auto-notified oncall. Details: region=us-west, model=redwood-gpt-3-small-quant, recent deploys: v2-canary.

pagerduty-bot: PD-54321 assigned to @ajay. Please acknowledge.

ajay: acked. I'm oncall and looking. Pulling up graphs now (p95 ~ 1.1s but p99 spike). Starting with autoscaler + recent rollout.

ajay: top checks: infra looks healthy, GPU mem stable, but request queue depth up on inference-prod pool.

maria: noted. Did the canary finish? We had a small flow for v2-canary this morning. Could be model CPU/kv cache regression.

sam: quick mitigation idea — temporarily reduce batching window + disable continuous batching so tail latency improves. We can flip the runtime flag via featuregate.

emily: also if the canary is suspect we can redirect traffic off the canary by bumping rollout to 0% or pin traffic to v1. Worth doing ASAP if rolling back is quick.

ajay: running `rdctl rollout list --service=inference-prod` now. 

ajay: output: v1=85%, v2-canary=15%. I'll cut canary to 0% if other mitigations don't help in 3 mins.

ajay: applying short-term mitigation: lowering batching window and disabling continuous batching for inference-prod. Command: ```
# temporary
rdctl config set inference-prod runtime.continuous_batching false
rdctl config set inference-prod runtime.batch_window_ms 10
```

ajay: applied. Observing metrics...

pagerduty-bot: PD-54321 acknowledged by ajay at 2345678920.

sam: also bumping replicas in dedicated pool to offset queue depth: `k scale deploy inference-prod --replicas=12 -n redwood-prod` (doing now).

maria: I can temporarily enable fallback routing to a lower-latency model `redwood-gpt-small-v1` for traffic above 1.2s to reduce customer impact. That's a config flip on the smart-router.

emily: going to notify CS (in /customer-success) and prepare a short blurb in case customers ask. Minimal impact so far but worth heads-up.

ajay: thanks. After the batching flip and scale, p99 dropped to ~1.6s (from 2.8s). Still above SLO but much better. Looking at traces now to see hot paths.

ajay: traces show many requests hitting KV cache misses for long prefixes — could be caused by v2's tokenization change.

sam: if tokenization changed, cache TTL/keys might not align. We should revert v2-canary to avoid cache churn.

ajay: rolling v2-canary down to 0% now: `rdctl rollout set inference-prod v2-canary=0`

ajay: rollback started.

maria: when rollback finishes, we should warm caches by priming common prompt prefixes via a small replay job. I'll queue a priming job to seed popular prefixes.

emily: CS notified and prepping comms: short internal note + customer-facing stub.

pagerduty-bot: PD-54321 update: acknowledged, mitigation in progress. Escalation policy triggered if not resolved in 15m.

ajay: rollback complete. Observability: p99 back to ~1.3s now. SLO still slightly above 1.5 in the tail earlier but trending down.

sam: nice. Re-enable continuous batching once stable? Might bring p99 up again though — test in canary first.

ajay: I will NOT re-enable continuous batching globally yet. We'll test in canary with v1 and see behavior. For now keep it off.

maria: prepping followup actions for the handoff: timeline, root cause hypothesis (v2 tokenization/cache key mismatch), actions taken (batching disabled, scaled replicas, rolled back canary, primed caches), impact (transient tail increase to 2.8s, % of requests above SLO ~0.8% at peak), next steps (canary test, code fix to tokenization/cache alignment, controlled re-enable).

ajay: ok paging @maria for takeover: I'm going to strip down remaining work and handoff in 5. If anything regresses ping PD and escalate.

emily: I'll coordinate with CS and send a short proactive note to the <customers> list: what happened, what we did, expected resolution timeline.

sam: adding runbook note: `runbook/latency-tail` updated with mitigation steps and commands used.

maria: ack takeover. Thanks @ajay. I'll monitor for 30m and coordinate next steps. Please put any post-incident findings in the ticket PD-54321.

ajay: handing off — summary: p99 spike caused by v2-canary tokenization mismatches causing cache churn + larger batches; quick fixes: disable continuous batching, lower batch window, scale replicas, rollback canary, seed cache. Current state: p99 ~1.25s, stable. PD-54321 remains open for postmortem.

emily: :thumbsup: CS brief sent (internal). Draft customer blurb ready, holding until Maria signs off.

pagerduty-bot: PD-54321 status: Mitigated. Assigned to maria for follow-up and retrospective.

maria: I'll start a short RCA doc and schedule a 30-min postmortem sync tomorrow. Leaving pinned actions: (1) fix tokenization/cache key mismatch, (2) add canary test that primes caches, (3) add auto-detect for cache miss storms, (4) refine autopager threshold so tiny transient blips don't auto-page unless queue depth also high.

ajay: closing my loop — will join postmortem. Good recovery, small customer impact.

emily: closing thread for now, will update when customers respond.

pagerduty-bot: PD-54321 will remain open until RCA complete.
